reading: The all-black input gets a one-cell frame of colour 8 along its outer border; the interior stays 0.

new_rows.name: edge
new_rows.datalog:
hmax(max(Y)) :- px(Y, X, C).
wmax(max(X)) :- px(Y, X, C).
edge(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), Y = 0.
edge(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), X = 0.
edge(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), hmax(H), Y = H.
edge(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), wmax(W), X = W.

why: every grid-border cell becomes 8 (constant colour); nothing else changes

reading: Row 1 starts with a short colour sequence (2-3 cells); the sequence is continued along the row at positions 0,1,3,6,10,15,21,28,... (gaps growing by one each time), cycling through the starting colours.

slots.sequence: the leading run of non-zero cells in the middle row, in order
slots.positions: triangular numbers n(n+1)/2 along the same row, until the row ends
slots.colour: the sequence colours cycled in order

why: every non-zero output cell sits at a triangular-number column of the middle row and its colour is seq[k mod len(seq)] for the k-th such position

reading: A horizontal line of 1s contains a few special cells (8 or 2). From each special cell a vertical bar grows upward: colour 8 gives two 1s capped by an 8 (3 cells above); colour 2 gives three 1s capped by a 2 (4 cells above).

slots.source: each non-1 cell in the full horizontal line of 1s
slots.cap: the source's own colour at the top cell

why: above each special cell of colour c there are L(c)-1 cells of 1 then one cell of c (L(8)=3, L(2)=4); all else unchanged

reading: Every 4 drops one row down. A 4 that thereby lands directly on top of the red (2) line shoots two diagonal rays of 4 up-left and up-right to the grid border.

frame.verb: drop one row, then emit diagonals on contact

slots.subject: each single 4 cell (markers), above or below the line
slots.trigger: the moved 4 is directly above the full row of 2s
slots.rays: diagonals up-left and up-right from the moved 4, colour 4, stopping at the grid border

why: each 4 is at (y+1,x); for those at the row just above the 2-line, all cells (y+1-k, x+-k) up to the border are 4

reading: A top bar (row 0) and a bottom bar (last row) are separated by a full red row. In the columns where both bars have cells, colour 4 fills the gap between the red row and the longer of the two bars.

new_rows.name: shared_gap
new_rows.datalog:
h(max(Y)) :- px(Y, X, C).
sepr(Y) :- cell(Y, X, C), C = 2.
top(X) :- cell(Y, X, C), Y = 0.
bot(X) :- h(H), cell(Y, X, C), Y = H.
nt(count(X)) :- top(X).
nb(count(X)) :- bot(X).
both(X) :- top(X), bot(X).
shared_gap(Y, X) :- both(X), px(Y, X, C), sepr(S), h(H), nt(A), nb(B), B > A, Y > S, Y < H.
shared_gap(Y, X) :- both(X), px(Y, X, C), sepr(S), nt(A), nb(B), A > B, Y > 0, Y < S.

why: cells in columns shared by both bars, strictly between the red row and the longer bar, become 4; nothing else changes

reading: A wall of 2s crosses the grid. Everything on the top side of the wall (4-connected to row 0 without crossing a 2) becomes 0; everything on the other side becomes the grid's other colour; the 2s stay.

frame.verb: clear one side, flood the other

slots.cleared side: non-2 cells 4-connected to the top row without passing a 2 -> 0
slots.filled side: all remaining non-2 cells -> the single non-0, non-2 colour of the input

why: output = 2 on input 2 cells, 0 on the top-connected region, colour c elsewhere

reading: Several open V-shaped 2 figures each enclose a hole; scattered 9 cells are removed and used to fill the hole of the one figure whose hole has exactly as many cells as there are 9s.

slots.markers: all 9 cells (count N), removed from their places
slots.holes: background cells enclosed inside each 2 figure's cup (between its arms)
slots.target: the figure whose hole size equals N

why: all 9s vanish from their positions; the hole with size N becomes 9; other figures unchanged

reading: A 7x7 box of 1s holds four key colours at its corners-inside (positions (1,1),(1,5),(5,1),(5,5)). Output is 7x7: each 3x3 corner block holds the 3x3 shape from the grid whose colour matches the key at that corner; the middle row and column are 0; shapes whose colour is not a key are ignored.

slots.key: the 7x7 box of 1s; its 4 non-1 cells give colour per quadrant
slots.pieces: the 3x3 single-colour objects outside the box
slots.layout: piece of key colour at (1,1) -> output block rows 0-2 cols 0-2, (1,5) -> rows 0-2 cols 4-6, (5,1) -> rows 4-6 cols 0-2, (5,5) -> rows 4-6 cols 4-6

why: each output quadrant equals the bounding box of the object whose colour sits at the matching key position

reading: A grid of 8 strips (period 3, with 0 holes) has one 6 block. In every strip other than the 6's own, 8 cells become 4 except inside a cone around the 6: the kept span along the strip is the 6's span widened by 2 cells per side for each further strip of distance (distance 1: same span; distance 2: +2; distance 3: +4).

frame.verb: recolour cells outside a cone from the seed

slots.strips: 2-wide stripes of 8 separated by full 0 lines (rows in pair 0, columns in pairs 1-2)
slots.subject: 8 cells in strips at distance d>=1 lying outside the seed's span extended by 2(d-1) cells on each side along the strip

why: only 8 cells change, all to 4, exactly those outside the widening cone and not in the seed's strip; 0 holes and the 6 block unchanged

reading: A line of marker cells lies outside a box parallel to a matching line inside the box. Each outside marker whose colour equals its partner inside the box moves perpendicular to the box until it touches the box wall; each marker that differs moves the other way to the far grid border.

frame.verb: move toward or away by comparison

slots.subject: each non-background cell in the free line outside the box
slots.partner: the cell in the same column (or row) on the box's inner line
slots.matching: move perpendicular toward the box, stopping adjacent to its wall
slots.different: move perpendicular away, to the grid border

why: each outside marker keeps its colour and column/row; it ends adjacent to the box iff it equals its inside partner, else on the far border
